messages.author: d359b7da0a3070cd
messages.subject: Affymetrix SNP IDs
parts:
In order to compare to results from another software system, I need
"Affymetrix SNP IDs" for each probe set. The annotation files I have --
e.g. "Mapping50K_Xba240.na27.annot.csv" start with the following
fields ...

"Probe Set ID","Affy SNP ID","dbSNP RS ID"

I am pretty sure that it is the second field that I want, but it is
blank (actually the missing value code, "---")

How can I work out the correspondence between Affy probe sets and
"Affy SNP IDs"?


Mike

messages.author: 185f4d4fdb048fb8
messages.subject: Re: [aroma.affymetrix] Affymetrix SNP IDs
parts:
On Thu, Dec 11, 2008 at 8:08 PM, Mike B <Michael...@csiro.au> wrote:
>
> In order to compare to results from another software system, I need
> "Affymetrix SNP IDs" for each probe set. The annotation files I have --
> e.g. "Mapping50K_Xba240.na27.annot.csv" start with the following
> fields ...
>
> "Probe Set ID","Affy SNP ID","dbSNP RS ID"
>
> I am pretty sure that it is the second field that I want, but it is
> blank (actually the missing value code, "---")
>
> How can I work out the correspondence between Affy probe sets and
> "Affy SNP IDs"?

The "Probe Set ID" field is what is in the CDF file, e.g.
getUnitNames(cdf, units=unitIdxs) and unitIdx <- indexOf(cdf,
"SNP_A-1780358"). That is what is typically used by other software,
e.g. Affymetrix GTC and dChip. It is the most convenient one, because
it is available in the CDF. The others you have to grab via the
NetAffx CSV file (or elsewhere).

The "dbSNP RS ID" can also be used to map across software.

I don't know the details of the "Affy SNP ID" field/column, but I
think it is an internal ID of Affymetrix not used elsewhere. From the
README file for corresponding CSV file: "1. Probe Set ID
(SNP_A-nnnnnnn) - Unique identifier for the probe set. 2. Affy SNP ID
(integer) - SNP identifier from Affymetrix. 3. dbSNP RS ID - SNP
identifier from dbSNP."

Cheers

/Henrik
